templates.name: Towns
templates.description: Make a town that fits the world around it.

spec.instructions: Ground the town in the world: who rules it, what it trades, what it fears. Give three named NPCs with a want each, two places to visit, and three rumours (one true, one half true, one false, marked for the DM).

steps.text: Search the library for the region, its rulers and nearby places.
Find the neighbouring places and keep trade routes and rivalries consistent.
Write the page with the sections below; put secrets in a DM-only callout.

spec.tone: Grounded and specific, with sensory details.

templates.name: NPCs
templates.description: Make a memorable NPC with a want, a secret and a voice.

spec.instructions: Every NPC gets a look in one line, a voice or habit the DM can act out, something they want, something they fear and a secret. Tie them to at least one place or faction already in the library.

steps.text: Search the library for the place and factions this NPC belongs to.
Write the page; keep the secret in a DM-only callout.

spec.tone: Vivid and playable at the table.

templates.name: Quests
templates.description: Turn an idea into a quest the party can follow.

spec.instructions: Give a hook the party can find, who asks and why, three steps with a choice or obstacle each, a twist, and what success and failure change in the world. Suggest a reward that fits the party's level.

steps.text: Search the library for the people and places involved.
Check nearby places for where steps can happen.
Write the quest page with the sections below.

templates.name: Factions
templates.description: Make a faction with goals, ranks and enemies.

spec.instructions: Give the faction a goal, a method, a leader, two notable members, ranks the party could earn, allies and enemies from the library, and what it wants from the party.

steps.text: Search the library for related factions, rulers and places.
Write the faction page; secrets go in a DM-only callout.

sections: What they want from the party

spec.instructions: Use the five-room structure: an entrance with a guardian, a puzzle or roleplay room, a setback or trick, the climax, and a reward or revelation. Give each room a short read-aloud, what is there, and how it changes if the party is noisy.

steps.text: Search the library for the dungeon's history and who lives there.
Write one section per room with read-aloud text in a quote.

templates.name: Session recap
templates.description: Write a recap of last session for the players.

spec.instructions: Write a short recap in past tense from the players' view: what they did, who they met, what they learned, and open threads. Never reveal DM-only facts.

steps.text: Read the session log and notes from the last session.
Write five to eight short paragraphs and a list of open threads.

spec.tone: Story-like, like the opening of a TV episode.

templates.name: Magic items
templates.description: Make a magic item with a history.

spec.instructions: Give the item a rarity, what it does in 5e terms (keep it balanced for the rarity), how it looks, who made it and a hook. Optional: a quirk or a curse marked for the DM.

steps.text: Search the library for the item's maker and places.
Write the item page with rules text in the Properties section.

templates.name: Monsters
templates.description: Make a monster that fits its region.

spec.instructions: Give the creature a niche in its region's ecology, signs the party sees before meeting it, tactics, a weakness clever players can find, and a stat block at the asked challenge rating.

steps.text: Search the library for the region and what lives there.
Check nearby places for where it hunts.
Write the page with a stat block in the Stats section.
